Title: ChatGPT-related research in medical education: A dual-database bibliometric review and science-mapping analysis, 2023 to 2026.
Abstract: The medical-education literature on ChatGPT has grown rapidly since 2023, but bibliometric patterns vary with database coverage, indexing fields, and the boundary used to define educational relevance. We examined publication growth, collaboration, and thematic development and assessed whether the leading patterns were stable under a stricter topic definition.

Title: From Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease to Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Mediterranean Diet.
Abstract: The knowledge structure and evolution of Mediterranean diet and fatty liver disease research from 1992 - 2025 were systematically characterized through bibliometric analysis, with additional examination of the terminological transition from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). A comprehensive bibliometric and knowledge graph analysis was performed on 725 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (1992-2025) using the bibliometrix R package, CiteSpace, and VOSviewer. Annual publication output increased rapidly from 2014 onward. Italy, Spain, and the United States led in the number of publications. Spanish research institutions were prominently represented among the most productive institutions. Nutrition-related journals dominated publication output, whereas hepatology journals, such as Hepatology and the Journal of Hepatology, occupied a central role in the cited literature. Keyword and topic analyses showed a shift from early nutrient-focused themes toward metabolic mechanisms and, more recently, clinical and lifestyle management. NAFLD transitioned from a motor theme (2005-2015) to a basic theme (2016-2025), while MASLD emerged as a recent research theme. Coronary heart disease research was a key focus during 2001-2020, whereas management-related research emerged as a rising hotspot beginning in 2022. Overall, the field evolved from nutrient-focused to management-oriented research, with terminology shifting from NAFLD to MASLD and current frontiers emphasizing clinical translation, gut microbiota, and multi-target mechanisms.

Title: The evolving landscape of artificial intelligence in cholecystectomy: a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis.
Abstract: To map the global research landscape and thematic evolution of artificial intelligence (AI)-related research in cholecystectomy and to identify major contributors, collaboration patterns, and intellectual foundations. English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After deduplication and eligibility screening, 559 publications were included. Publication trends, scientific collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, conceptual structure, thematic evolution, and co-citation and citation-burst patterns were analyzed using bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and Python. Research activity increased markedly in recent years, with 424 publications (75.8%) appearing between 2022 and 2025. China contributed the largest publication output, whereas the United States received the highest total citations. Keyword and conceptual-structure analyses identified research domains involving AI and computational methods, surgical workflow and intraoperative visual analysis, and computer-vision-based applications. Thematic evolution suggested a progression from early workflow- and convolutional-neural-network-related research toward machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, surgical phase recognition, and more recent transformer-related approaches. Twinanda et al. [1] showed the strongest citation burst and occupied a prominent position in the reference co-citation network. AI-related research in cholecystectomy has expanded rapidly and become increasingly diverse in its methodological and application-oriented focus. Current bibliometric patterns suggest growing attention to workflow analysis, computer vision, surgical phase recognition, and newer model architectures. Further multicenter validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed to determine whether these developments translate into generalizable and clinically meaningful applications.

Title: Global research trends and emerging hotspots in probiotics and children's neurodevelopment: a bibliometric and visualized analysis (1998-2026, partial year).
Abstract: Research on the role of probiotics in children's neurodevelopment has expanded rapidly, yet a quantitative synthesis of this interdisciplinary field is lacking. Common keyword synonyms were merged prior to network construction. Annual publication output increased steadily from 1998 to 2015 and accelerated sharply after 2020, reaching a peak in 2025. Title: Neuroinflammation-Associated Synaptic Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Dual-Database Parallel Bibliometric Analysis.
Abstract: Neuroinflammation-associated synaptic dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a convergent pathological process across neurodegenerative diseases; however, the development, knowledge structure, and emerging directions of this interdisciplinary field remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a structured bibliometric workflow for retrieving, curating, and analyzing bibliographic records from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus using a dual-database parallel design. Publications from 2000-2025 were independently retrieved, filtered, and processed, yielding 1,841 records from Web of Science and 2,429 records from Scopus. Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, BiblioVista, and Scimago Graphica were used to characterize publication trends, disciplinary distributions, international collaboration, author and institutional networks, core journals and references, keyword co-occurrence, citation bursts, and thematic evolution. Both databases showed sustained growth in research output, with higher publication activity observed after 2015. The United States and China were among the leading contributors and highly connected participants in international collaboration networks. The intellectual and conceptual structures of the field were frequently characterized by recurring themes involving neuroinflammation, microglia, synaptic dysfunction, complement-mediated synaptic pruning, oxidative stress, synaptic plasticity, and neurodegenerative disease pathology. Temporal analyses showed evolving patterns in research themes, with increasing representation of studies related to neuroimmune synapse interactions and synaptic vulnerability. By retaining the two databases as independent analytical corpora rather than directly merging their records, this workflow enables descriptive comparison of shared and database-specific bibliometric patterns. The workflow provides a structured framework for mapping neuroinflammation-synapse research and may be adapted to other interdisciplinary biomedical fields.

Title: Bibliometric Analysis of Sustainable Practices in Hotels and Homestays: Trends, Themes, and Future Research Directions.
Abstract: Sustainability has emerged as a critical concern in the hospitality sector, however there is a lack of a systematic review of the academic literature on sustainability in hotels and homestays. The rise of environmental concerns, responsible tourist practices, and the growing importance of sustainable hospitality have significantly expanded the academic interest in this area of study. This study provides a bibliometric review of the literature on sustainability in hotels and homestays to identify patterns of growth, dominant themes, and research gaps to guide future research and policy.

Title: A bibliometric study of social isolation and biomarkers of ageing.
Abstract: Research on social isolation suggests that psychosocial factors are not only associated with adverse mental health conditions but also associated with various neurobiological and immunological processes. The physiological mechanisms underlying the health effects of social isolation can be indicated by various biomarkers such as cortisol, cytokines, C-reactive protein, telomere length, DNA methylation, epigenetic clocks. Though the research concerning the relationship between social isolation and biomarkers of ageing is expanding, a detailed and comprehensive picture of global research trends, emerging patterns of themes is limited. The present study attempts to examine the scientific production, influential contributions of authors, evolution of major research themes on social isolation and biomarkers of ageing. Scopus database has been used to retrieve relevant publications using a structured search strategy. Systematic and transparent data extraction, filtering, and cleaning procedures resulted in construction of the final bibliometric dataset. The records were published during the time period of 1971-2026 and included only scientific articles, review and English-language documents. The final dataset consisted of 1973 publications. Bibliometrix packages in Rstudio are used to conduct performance and conceptual mapping. The findings of the study are represented under performance indicators, thematic mapping, evolution of themes during different time slices and factorial analysis. The results reflected the major contributions from developed countries and leading institutions showing scholarly interest in the biological consequences of social isolation. The future research can be directed towards finding relationships between biopsychosocial determinants of overall well-being of the person, developing intervention strategies aimed at reducing the negative consequences of social isolation.

Title: Dweck's Growth Mindset Theory in Health Professions Education: A Bibliometric Review.
Abstract: Carol Dweck's Growth Mindset Theory (GMT) has gained increasing attention in health professions education (HPE), yet its development has not been comprehensively mapped. This first bibliometric review analyzed 142 HPE articles identified through a Scopus search and Bibliometrix analysis. Publications increased substantially after 2016, with rapid growth following 2020. Commonly associated concepts included resilience, competency-based education, motivation, and self-regulation. The United States produced the most publications and citations, and medicine, nursing, and pharmacy were the most represented professions. Although GMT scholarship in HPE is expanding, greater collaboration and more robust research designs are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

Abstract: Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) is still a major cause of mortality and morbidity all over the world. Title: Nanomaterial applications and emerging trends in osteoarthritis from 2005 to 2025.
Abstract: Osteoarthritis is a major cause of pain, disability, and long-term functional limitation worldwide. With population aging and the increasing disease burden, there is growing interest in how emerging biomaterials are being applied to OA-related research and intervention. Among these materials, nanomaterials have attracted particular attention because of their potential roles in intra-articular delivery, cartilage targeting and retention, inflammation regulation, oxidative stress modulation, imaging or detection, and cartilage repair. However, a systematic bibliometric analysis that maps the broader OA-related application landscape of nanomaterials remains limited. This study analyzed publications from the Web of Science Core Collection from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2025. Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace were used to examine publication trends, national and institutional collaboration, author networks, keyword evolution, journal distribution, and highly cited literature. The analysis included 2,283 publications. Annual publication output showed an overall upward trend, progressing from an exploratory stage during 2005-2013 to steady growth during 2014-2019 and accelerated expansion during 2020-2025. China produced the largest number of publications, whereas the United States and several European countries showed stronger international collaboration. The main research themes were nanomaterial-based delivery systems, cartilage repair, inflammation regulation, oxidative stress control, sustained release, and regenerative applications. Keyword evolution indicated that the field has shifted from basic cartilage-related research toward more application-oriented topics such as smart drug carriers, cartilage-targeted delivery, ROS-responsive systems, nanozymes, ferroptosis-related mechanisms, and stem-cell-related strategies. Core journals included International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Chemical Engineering Journal, International Journal of Nanomedicine, Biomaterials, and Acta Biomaterialia. Local citation patterns further suggested that this field is supported by both OA-specific research and broader biomaterials or nanomedicine-related knowledge. Overall, nanomaterial applications in Osteoarthritis have developed into an interdisciplinary and increasingly application-oriented field. Future studies should focus on improving targeting specificity, intra-articular retention, biosafety, reproducibility, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation. This bibliometric study provides a structured overview of the broader OA-related nanomaterial application landscape, its knowledge structure, research hotspots, and future translational priorities.

Title: Plant Disease and Phytopathogen Research in Central Asia: A Bibliometric Mapping of Research Trends, Collaboration, and Emerging Directions.
Abstract: Plant diseases and phytopathogenic threats pose significant challenges to agricultural productivity and food security in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. This study aimed to characterize research development, scientific productivity, collaboration patterns, intellectual structure, and emerging trends in plant disease and phytopathogen research. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using 505 Scopus-indexed publications from 1994 to 2026, covering 253 sources and 2485 authors. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were used for performance analysis and science mapping, including citation, co-authorship, collaboration, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, historiograph, and keyword co-occurrence analyses. Research output showed an annual growth rate of 11.65%, with an average of 13.94 citations per publication. Kazakhstan (143 publications) and Uzbekistan (82 publications) were the leading contributors, while international co-authorship accounted for 33.66% of publications. Three major research directions were identified: wheat disease resistance and molecular breeding, plant pathogens and fungal biodiversity, and plant-associated microorganisms, microbiology, and phylogenetic characterization. Recent trends indicate increasing attention to molecular and genomic approaches, microbiome research, and deep learning. Overall, research in Central Asia is becoming increasingly multidisciplinary, highlighting the need to integrate genomic diagnostics, pathogen surveillance, molecular breeding, biological control, and data-driven approaches for sustainable plant disease management.

Title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

Title: Global trends and thematic evolution in online consultation with digital health technologies: Implications for future implementation and policy development.
Abstract: Online consultation has become a mainstream element of digital health within telemedicine, seeing rapid growth during the COVID-19 pandemic. Video, telephone, and secure messaging are extensively used for clinical advice, assessments, and follow-ups. However, the adoption of these technologies remains inconsistent, particularly in regions with limited infrastructure and workforce capacity. Key challenges include patient engagement, integration into clinical workflows, and the efficient allocation of resources. This bibliometric analysis covers 2,426 English-language journal articles indexed in the Science Citation Index Expanded (SCI-Expanded) within the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) (1990-2025). Utilizing VOSviewer and the bibliometrix package, we mapped publication growth, international collaborations, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution, with country-specific trajectories examined for the leading contributors. Countries were ranked via full counting, and joinpoint regression identified inflection points in annual publication output. Publication output grew steadily over the past 35 years, accelerating significantly after 2018, with a sharp peak from 2019 to 2022. The United States, England, China, Canada, Australia, and Germany were the main contributors and central hubs in international collaboration. The thematic focus shifted from early feasibility studies to service management, quality and outcome evaluation, barriers to implementation, equity considerations, and post-pandemic integration into standard care pathways. Country-specific trends were evident: the United States focused on telemedicine models and reimbursement mechanisms, England concentrated on primary care and general practice, and China experienced rapid growth in telehealth research post-2018. The literature on online consultation has evolved from proof-of-concept studies to a system-wide focus on management, evaluation, and large-scale implementation. These variations reflect differences in health system organization, regulation, reimbursement policies, and digital readiness across countries. Long-term reimbursement strategies, interoperable digital infrastructures, and equity-oriented service design may support the sustainable implementation of online consultation services.

Title: Multi-Sensor SLAM and 3D Robotic Mapping in Confined Environments: A Systematic Review of Perception, Localization, and Autonomous Exploration.
Abstract: Low illumination, structural repetition, absence of satellite-based positioning signals, and communication constraints in confined spaces pose significant challenges for robotic localization, 3D mapping, and autonomous exploration. Following PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines, this review included 166 studies identified through searches of Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect. Bibliometric analyses-including publication and citation statistics, keyword co-occurrence, cluster classification, and temporal evolution-were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Bibliometrix. These quantitative approaches were complemented by content analysis to evaluate application scenarios, technical capabilities, and validation maturity. The findings indicate that existing research predominantly focuses on Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), LiDAR perception, and multi-sensor fusion, with a strong emphasis on geometric mapping and localization. Conversely, investigations into semantic understanding, autonomous decision-making, risk assessment, and safe return mechanisms remain relatively insufficient. Validation methodologies are primarily limited to simulations and laboratory tests, resulting in scarce empirical evidence regarding real-world scenarios and long-term deployments. Based on these insights, this paper discusses technological evolution through the lens of scenario complexity, autonomy, and deployment maturity, and identifies prospective research directions such as semantic mapping, embodied intelligence, foundation models, multi-robot collaboration, risk-aware navigation, and standardized testing platforms. This review provides a reference framework for advancing robots in enclosed environments from geometric perception toward autonomous exploration.

Title: Research and therapeutic status of NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease: A bibliometric study from 2000 to 2024.
Abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease (NERD) is a chronic inflammatory condition clinically characterized by the triad of asthma, nasal polyps, and hypersensitivity reactions after aspirin ingestion. It is a distinct syndrome that is closely associated with eosinophilic infiltration of respiratory tissues and excessive production of cysteinyl leukotrienes. Research on NERD is characterized by fragmented knowledge, an incomplete understanding of its underlying mechanisms, and a lack of standardized approaches for its diagnosis and treatment. Title: bibliolatam: Latin American Bibliographic Data Adapters for 'bibliometrix'
Abstract: bibliolatam is an open-source R package developed by the Brazilian Research Archive Network (BRAN Org) that bridges Latin American, Caribbean, and Iberian Diamond Open Access scientific repositories into mainstream bibliometric pipelines (bibliometrix, biblioshiny, VOSviewer, Gephi) and standalone data workflows. Scientific Context & Motivation Commercial citation indexes (Web of Science, Scopus) systematically under-represent scientific production from the Global South. In Latin America, regional science has historically flourished under publicly funded, non-commercial Diamond Open Access infrastructures (SciELO, Redalyc, SPELL) and national thesis/dissertation repositories (BDTD, Oasisbr, LA Referencia). Because mainstream scientometric packages restrict their native parsers to commercial Global North formats, regional research is often excluded from large-scale quantitative science studies. bibliolatam fills this structural gap by providing modular parsers, automated REST API clients, and entity resolution algorithms designed specifically for regional data semantics. Supported Repositories & Data Coverage SciELO: Automated Crossref API query (10.1590), tabular CSV, and NLM/JATS XML parsing with extraction into standard WoS-format CR tags. BDTD: Automated VuFind REST API search across Brazilian graduate programs, degree filtering, and academic advisors mapped to RP. Oasisbr: Multi-institutional Brazilian open science repository ingestion via VuFind API and tabular files. LA Referencia: Federated queries connecting 12 Latin American national repository networks. Redalyc & AmeliCA: Ingestion of BibTeX, RIS, and CSV exports with Hispanic compound surname normalization. SPELL / ANPAD: Ingestion of administration, accounting, and economics literature. Key Architectural Capabilities Federated Omnisearch (omnisearch_bibliolatam): Query 4 regional platforms simultaneously with API-level year bounds and deduplication. Entity Resolution (merge_bibliolatam): Resolves records by canonical DOI and fuzzy Levenshtein title distance. Author Normalization (normalize_authors): Handles Brazilian generational suffixes (Junior, Filho, Neto), compound particles, and institutional authors. Strict S3 bibliometrixDB Contract: 100% compliant with standard WoS tags without data fabrication (NA/0). Standalone Trilingual GUI (run_app): Interactive Shiny dashboard (EN / PT / ES) with 1-click export to CSV and .RData.

Title: Educational data mining and STEM education: a bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix
Abstract: Objective: To analyze the Scopus-indexed scientific production on educational data mining as a STEM teaching strategy in secondary education, with emphasis on the gaps for the teaching of biological sciences. Methodology: A descriptive, retrospective bibliometric review, reported according to PRISMA version 2020, was conducted on 128 articles published between 2014 and 2026; the analysis was performed with Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny using production indicators, Bradford's and Lotka's laws, co-authorship and country collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, and the classification of studies by level, discipline, technique, and design. Results: 58.6% of the documents were published between 2023 and 2026; production was dispersed across 75 journals, and 88.9% of the authors signed a single document. Collaboration networks were fragmented and centered on the United States, China, and Spain, with no Colombian affiliations. Learning analytics articulated the field; only 7.8% of the studies were declared integrated STEM, and only 4.7% mentioned biology. Conclusions: Production is growing but dispersed, and teaching proposals that bring the analysis of authentic data applied to the natural sciences into Latin American contexts are needed.

Title: Navigating Bibliometric Analysis: A Stepwise Approach Using Bibliometrix Library in R Software
Abstract: Bibliometric analysis is a powerful tool for evaluating research trends, identifying key contributors, and mapping the intellectual structure of a scientific field. With the increasing volume of academic publications, systematic approaches are essential for deriving meaningful insights from scholarly data. This paper presents a stepwise approach to conducting bibliometric analysis using the Biblioshiny app in Bibliometrix package in R software. Bibliometrix provides a comprehensive framework for importing, processing, and visualizing bibliographic data from databases such as Web of Science, Scopus and Dimensions.ai.The paper outlines key stages of bibliometric analysis, including data collection, preprocessing, descriptive statistics, network analysis, and thematic mapping. It also explores citation analysis, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence patterns to uncover research trends and collaboration dynamics. By leveraging R's powerful statistical capabilities, this approach ensures reproducibility and flexibility in bibliometric studies.

Title: TREND RISET EDIBLE PLANT ANALISIS BIBLIOMETRIX MENGGUNAKAN BIBLIOSHINY
Abstract: Perkembangan penelitian mengenai edible plant menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan dalam dua dekade terakhir, sejalan dengan meningkatnya perhatian global terhadap ketahanan pangan, pemanfaatan biodiversitas, dan kajian etnobotani. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan perkembangan, tren, dan pola publikasi ilmiah terkait edible plant menggunakan analisis bibliometrik. Metode bibliometrik digunakan untuk menelaah produksi, pertumbuhan, dan distribusi publikasi ilmiah dengan pendekatan deskriptif berdasarkan data Scopus yang mencakup 1.369 dokumen yang diterbitkan pada rentang tahun 2005–2025. Hasil analisis dari berbagai aspek, seperti Main Information, Annual Scientific Production, Average Citations per Year, Most Relevant Sources, Authors' Local Impact by H-Index, Top Authors Production Over The Time, Corresponding Authors’ Countries, Most Global Cited Documents, Word Cloud, dan Trend Topics, memberikan gambaran komprehensif mengenai dinamika penelitian edible plant. Temuan utama menunjukkan adanya peningkatan publikasi yang stabil, dominasi artikel ilmiah, kontribusi besar dari lebih dari lima ribu penulis, serta kemunculan topik-topik penting seperti wild edible plants, pangan fungsional, dan etnobotani. Title: Comparative methodological analysis of Bibexcel and Bibliometrix in Scientific Co-authorship Networks: evidence from the Brazilian Synchrotron
Abstract: This study compares Bibexcel and Bibliometrix in co-authorship network analysis, focusing on transparency, automation, and reproducibility. Using 364 Web of Science articles linked to the Brazilian Synchrotron (LNLS), the research evaluates data extraction, preprocessing, and visualization workflows. Results indicate that Bibexcel provides greater transparency and control, while Bibliometrix offers automation and efficiency. The comparison highlights methodological implications for open science and scientific sovereignty, emphasizing how the choice of tool affects reproducibility, accessibility, and interpretation of collaborative networks.

Title: Bibliometric Analysis of Knowledge Sharing in Virtual Teams: Approaches With Bibliometrix R‐Package
Abstract: ABSTRACT This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of the literature on knowledge sharing in virtual teams, using the Bibliometrix R‐package 4.2 to analyze data from the Scopus database covering the period 2014–2024. It aims to provide a comprehensive overview of publication trends, identify prolific authors, institutions, and countries, highlight dominant keywords, and subject areas, and map the intellectual, social, and conceptual structures shaping the field. The analysis reveals major thematic clusters centered on trust‐building, collaborative practices, and the integration of advanced technologies, such as virtual and augmented reality, in virtual teamwork. Notably, the findings emphasize the overrepresentation of North American and Asian contexts, while research from developing countries remains limited, despite the unique cultural, economic, and technological challenges these environments present. This geographical imbalance points to critical areas for future investigation. The study confirms the interdisciplinary and global scope of the topic, with the USA and China emerging as leading contributors, and smaller nations offering distinct regional perspectives. As one of the first bibliometric reviews focused exclusively on this domain, this research offers valuable insights into its evolution and identifies promising avenues for future exploration. It invites scholars to address existing gaps and to investigate collaborative dynamics in multicultural and digitally evolving environments, while leveraging emerging technologies to enhance knowledge exchange in virtual teams.

Title: Trends and insights in emotional intelligence research in business: A Bibliometrix Analysis from 2020 to 2024
Abstract: Emotional intelligence in business continues to change with the dynamism of emerging global challenges and innovations. Awareness of these current trends is very important for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers in the field. This article presents a complete bibliometric analysis of emotional intelligence (EI) in the business field from 2020 to 2024. The publication trend, collaboration network, pattern of citations, diversity of content, different types of documents, and core sources were analyzed using the Bibliometrix tool. The outcome of this analysis may prove very valuable on productivity trends, changes in citation impact, and changes in thematic foci. Results reflect increasing interest in EI from 2020 to 2022 and decreasing research output after this year, which can be explained by changes in the research funding landscape and current international events, such as the COVID-19 outbreak. This indicates the importance of international collaborations because the average coauthorship for each paper is high, and a significant part of the coauthorships are international. Published articles in 2021 reflect the publication relevance of EI during this period. The prominent themes are the application of EI to integrate recent technological advances, such as artificial intelligence, and its corollary of application in crisis management.

Title: Graph Theory for Blockchain: Direction for Future through Bibliometrix Analysis
Abstract: Graph theory is essential to blockchain technology, as all transactions can be viewed as edges between nodes, where nodes are addresses or blocks.Although blockchain and graph theory are becoming increasingly popular for research in security, scalability, and consensus mechanisms, the intersection of these two areas has yet to be mapped using comprehensive bibliometric analysis.This study investigates 1,250 peer-reviewed articles (2017-2025) from Scopus and systematically evaluates the literature on graph theory and blockchain to identify significant research trends, collaboration patterns, and areas of thematic clusters.Findings indicate that 70% of contributions are from China and the US, and there is little to no crossover between theoretical graph computing research and applied blockchain research.New methods (e.g., Graph Neural Networks) are emerging but have not yet been widely used in a blockchain context.The keyword analysis produced four thematic application areas for blockchain: consensus mechanisms, security and fraud detection, scalability examples, and smart contract examples.This is the first comprehensive and systematic mapping of graph theory in blockchain, offers a comprehensive insight into the field, highlights research gaps that research can focus on, and provides insight for interdisciplinary research between mathematics and distributed systems in the future.

Title: Coğrafi İmgelemleri Saymak: Bibliometrix Üzerinden Sistematik Bir Analiz
Abstract: Bu makale, coğrafi imgelemler literatürünü bibliyometrik olarak incelemektedir. Web of Science (WoS) platformundan elde edilen 834 yayına ilişkin bibliyometrik verileri Bibliyometrix aracılığıyla analiz eden çalışma, üç araştırma sorusuna cevap aramaktadır: (1) Coğrafi imgelemler yazar, kaynak ülke, yayın yeri, atıf gibi tanımlayıcı parametreler doğrultusunda nasıl bir görünüme sahiptir? (2) Coğrafi imgelemler literatüründe öne çıkan araştırma temaları nelerdir? (3) Coğrafi imgelemler literatüründe gelişime açık yükselen temalar hangileridir? Buna göre, 1976-2025 aralığında, coğrafi imgelem konulu yayınlar nicel bir büyüme eğilimi sergilerken; bu eğilim dergi, yazar, kurum, ülke, atıf gibi parametreler bakımından Anglo-Amerikan merkezli bir bağlam taşımaktadır. Bununla birlikte jeopolitik, göç ve edebiyat en çok çalışılan temalar olarak tespit edilirken; sağlık, pedagoji, coğrafi bilgi sistemleri, etik, ilişkisel mekan ve küresel güney başlıkları da yükselen temalar olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Çalışma, coğrafi imgelemlerin tematik çeşitlilikle kendisini gösteren bütüncül ve kapsayıcı bağlamının, alternatif kuramsal çerçevelerin inşası için model olarak kullanılabileceği ile sonuçlanmaktadır.

Title: Bibliometrix Analysis of Research on Digitalization and Educational Technology (2017-2024)
Abstract: Digitalization is becoming a key factor in improving the quality and competitiveness of vocational education, especially in technical universities. It allows for the introduction of modern teaching solutions and supports practical vocational education. This study uses bibliometric analysis to study the dynamics of research related to digital pedagogy and educational technologies. The dataset consists of 93 Scopus indexed publications from 2017 to 2024, which were analyzed using Excel, MapChart and VOSviewer to identify key patterns, influential contributors and new research directions. The results show a significant increase in scientific interest, with the number of publications increasing by more than 65% during the observed period. All reviewed articles were published in English, and the highest contributions came from Germany, the Russian Federation, Finland and China. The analysis shows a clear shift towards technology -enabled learning models that reflect global efforts to modernize vocational education. Thematic trends indicate a strong focus on e- learning ecosystems, the development of digital competencies for teachers, and innovative teaching approaches. Bibliometric mapping highlights active research networks and leading sources that are shaping academic debates on digital transformation. Overall, the findings provide valuable empirical evidence for policy development, strategic planning, and curriculum renewal in vocational education. The study provides historical insights and future-oriented guidance, helping educators, researchers, and decision-makers to promote effective digital transformation in the field.

Title: Retirement Plan and Its Relation with Financial Behavior: a Bibliometrix Analysis
Abstract: This research uses bibliometric analysis to explore the relationships between retirement and financial behavior. A comprehensive search yielded 5202 documents spanning from 1946 to 2024. Utilizing bibliometric techniques, including co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and citation network analysis, this study examines the evolution of research trends, key themes, and intellectual structures within the field. Findings reveal a growing interest in the intersection of retirement and financial behavior, with an increasing emphasis on topics such as retirement planning, financial literacy, savings behavior, and investment strategies. Co-citation analysis identifies seminal works and influential authors, while keyword co-occurrence analysis highlights prominent themes and concepts. Citation network analysis elucidates the interconnectedness of research topics and the dissemination of knowledge within the field. Limitations, including scope constraints and publication biases, are acknowledged, and future research directions are proposed to further advance our understanding of retirement and financial behavior dynamics. This study contributes to the existing literature by providing a comprehensive overview of research trends and thematic patterns, informing future research agendas and policy initiatives aimed at promoting financial wellbeing in retirement.

Title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Human Resource Analytics Using Vosviewer and R Studio Bibliometrix
Abstract: Purpose: HR Analytics is a growing topic and an area of interest for many researchers across India and worldwide. This study aims to emphasize collaboration among authors, universities, and countries in the area and, identify the most prominent authors, journals, universities, and countries to learn about the research challenges on which researchers are currently working in HR Analytics. Methodology: This study systematically examined the Human Resource Analytics study area by conducting a bibliometric study of 266 Scopus articles from 2012 to July 2023. We conducted a various analyses using VOSviewer and R Studio Bibliometrix. Findings: The finding of the study shows that India, the US, Germany, and the Netherlands are the top countries in HR Analytics publications; collaborations between countries and universities focusing on HR Analytics are minimal. Angrave et al. and Marler and Boudreau were the most prominent authors. Originality/ Value: The findings of this study provide valuable information to academicians, scholars and researchers to understand the research trends in Human Resource Analytics. Title: Behavioural Economics and Entrepreneurial Decision Making: Output Results From Scopus and AI Bibliometrix
Abstract: This research through a scopus corpus (2016–2026) is an emerging study employing an AI-assisted Bibliometrix tool, that the chapter presents a brief but comprehensive summary of the field of behavioural economics applied to decisions in the domain of entrepreneurship. We analyse growth and sources as well as co-word matrices, and identify a behavioural–decision core revolving around cognitive mechanisms (biases, dual-process balance), social embeddedness (funding ties, team dynamics), and AI-enabled supports (generative and explainable systems). Outputs of science-mapping—annual production, thematic and trend-topic maps, and source distributions—seem to unfold three interrelated waves: human–AI symbiosis in opportunity work, governance-by-design through explainable and contestable interfaces, and digitally mediated choice architectures for sustainability.

Title: AI BIBLIOMETRIX 5.0 FOR CULTURAL FACTORS, ORGANISATIONAL, AND LEADERSHIP ON DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND EDUCATIONAL EFFICIENCY
Abstract: This study conducts a bibliometric analysis to examine the interconnected influences of cultural factors, organisational dynamics, and leadership capabilities on digital transformation and educational efficiency, drawing on a dataset generated with AI Bibliometrix 5.0 to map the field's intellectual landscape. The results show consistent growth in scientific production from 2016 to 2025, reflecting an increasing worldwide interest in digital transformation across multiple educational scenarios, with significant scientific output originating mainly from the USA, the UK, Australia, Indonesia, and China. Network co-occurrence and word-cloud map analyses demonstrate that research topics are increasingly converging on digital innovation, organisational readiness, leadership competencies, and cultural flexibility, emphasising how these factors together may determine successful transformative outcomes. Analysis of trend topics also reveals that digitalisation processes in education are highly influenced by institutional culture, the governance model, and leadership approach, which, in turn, impact the level of technology adoption and the institution’s operational effectiveness. The thematic map and the factorial analysis evidence significant shifts from basic research on digital adoption toward more mature themes focused on organisational efficiency, strategic alignment, and performance enhancement. The bibliometric results confirm that cultural openness, organisational agility, and transformative leadership are interrelated factors that substantially contribute to the positive outcomes of the digital transformation and the potential to improve educational effectiveness. The paper makes a contribution through a systematic, data-based synthesis of research patterns and thematic trends, thereby paving the way for further empirical research and policy development in digitally supported education.

Title: Research Progress on Intelligent Detection of Plant Diseases and Pests: A Bibliometric Analysis Via Bibliometrix
Abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 233 publications from 2016–2025 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, aiming to map the global research landscape of intelligent detection of plant disease and pest. Using Bibliometrix and related tools, the study examines publication trends, leading countries and institutions, collaboration networks, and thematic structures. Results show a continuous growth in research output, with China, the United States, and India emerging as major contributors, and China leading in both productivity and citation impact. Keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping reveal deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, and object detection as central research themes, while remote sensing, drones, and smart farming represent rapidly developing fronts. Burst-term analysis further highlights lightweight models, vision transformers, and real-time detection as emerging technological directions. This study provides valuable insights into the knowledge evolution, research hotspots, and future pathways of AI-driven plant disease and pest detection.

Title: Analyzing 6G Wireless Evolution Using Scopus Data and AI-Powered Bibliometrix Frameworks
Abstract: By analyzing the results of prior work in standard development organizations, particularly 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), this work offers a fact-based overview of the sixth-generation (6G) wireless evolution, encapsulated in the growth, structures, and trajectories of research in a standards-aware context, by merging Scopus coverage with an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Bibliometrix workflow. Adopting PRISMA-consistent reporting and reproducible scripts, we investigate the 2015–2026 corpus (541 documents from 133 sources) and observe a persistent rise (27.11% annual growth rate), significant influence (26.08 citations per document), and extensive collaboration (9.73 co-authors per paper; 41.96% international), suggesting a maturing and increasingly global field. Co-word and thematic/factorial analyses highlight three interrelated poles: (i) a well-established systems core based on 5G-based building blocks that ensure scalability and stability; (ii) radio-frontier enablers THz, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), and (X)L-MIMO extending the physical design domain; and (iii) intelligence and purpose AI-native orchestration integrated sensing and communications, together with semantic communications that reorient the network toward a perception-aware, goal-based system. The collaboration map shows a polycentric organization around multi-hub corridors and regional clusters, reflecting possible resilience against a single point of failure and a conducive environment for large-scale experimentation. These results, taken together, imply that electromagnetic radiation (EmR) value in the near term will be driven more by isolated breakthroughs and less by disciplined coalescence, as EmR brings high-perspective radios into the Open, AI-deep residual network (DRN), and semantics-aware service goals where energy, trust, and security are first-order design constraints. With the introduction of quantification and open methodology, this paper provides a 6G snapshot to ground the literature and a living anchor for future incremental updates, which is key to allow scholars, engineers, and decision makers to view shifts in salience, corroborate trajectories of engineering, and prioritize investments full speed on the track from ability blueprints to deployable 6G systems.

Title: A Bibliometrix Analysis on Clean Energy Towards Shaping a Sustainable India using R Studio
Abstract: The transition to clean energy is a key factor in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), as well as combating climate change-related issues. India, with its rapidly growing economy, has distinctly increased investment in renewable energy sources and sustainability studies to meet an ever-growing energy demand while simultaneously reducing environmental implications. The paper is a bibliometrical work titled A Bibliometrix Analysis on Clean Energy Towards Shaping a Sustainable India using R Studio, which provides a systematic research investigation of trends in research, the development of themes, and patterns of collaboration within the field of clean energy. The given work includes an extensive review of the publications associated with the topic of clean energy in 2015-2025, concerning the number of 894 research articles based on 346 different sources. To have greater coverage and reliability, the data set has been compiled by combining records in both the Scopus and Web of Science databases. With the help of the Bibliometrix package of R Studio, the paper will index key performance indicators, co-authorship networks, and patterns related to the keyword co-occurrence to identify the influential contributors, emergent themes, and changing directions in research that are influencing the sustainable energy picture in India. Results have shown that the volume of publications has been growing at an annual rate of 46.43 per cent, thus reflecting a strong increase in the scholarly interest regarding the clean-energy and sustainability transitions in the Indian context. The key areas of research defined are clean energy, renewable energy, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), strategies of mitigation of climate change, and energy policy frameworks. Prominent scholars are developing community projects that create strong transnational connections, thus making interdisciplinary fusion. Thematic mapping has become a rising technique in analysis, and the core motor themes have been on SDGs and renewable-energy technologies. The paper ends with policy implications and indicates a lack of diverse future research directions required to continue to develop the scholarly literature of clean energy in India.

Title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Public-Private Partnerships in Forest Management Using Bibliometrix R-Studio
Abstract: The paper thereby joins the discussion on the fast-changing research landscape of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in forest management, providing a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. A dataset of 241 documents is retrieved from the Scopus database, whose analyses are done using advanced bibliometric tools available within the Bibliometrix package in R Studio. The study maps the intellectual structure of the field, identifies its key themes, and traces their evolution from 1987 to 2024. The bibliometric approach allows for the identification of core authors, influential journals, leading institutions, and geographical distribution of contributions, thereby painting a clear picture of the knowledge dynamics within the domain. The findings underline the central place PPP holds in the face of such global challenges as climate change, preservation of biodiversity, and sustainable development but bring into sharper focus the governance and institutional frameworks that underpin these partnerships. Special attention is paid to the policy discourses and academic debates surrounding PPP arrangements, especially in developing countries where forest governance is often contested. Title: The Impact of Armed Conflict on Education: Output Results From Lens and AI Bibliometrix
Abstract: This chapter conducts a bibliometric analysis of global research on armed conflict and its impact on education, using publication data extracted from Lens.org and processed with AI-supported bibliometric techniques. The results reveal a steadily expanding scholarly focus on how conflict disrupts learning systems, exacerbates inequalities, and undermines long-term human capital development. Co-authorship networks highlight strong interdisciplinary collaboration among researchers in education, peace studies, public policy, and international development. Keyword co-occurrence mapping identifies dominant thematic clusters, including “education in emergencies,” “child protection,” “school-based resilience,” and “post-conflict reconstruction,” reflecting a diverse and evolving research agenda. Citation patterns show that influential works increasingly emphasize evidence-based interventions, the role of international organizations, and the long-term socio-economic consequences of educational disruption.

Title: Geoparks and the Development of Ecotourism: A Systematic Synthesis of Research Using Bibliometrix and PRISMA Approaches
Abstract: This study presents a systematic literature review combined with a bibliometric analysis of ecotourism within geoparks. A dataset of 194 scientific publications was retrieved from seven academic databases: Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Nature Journals, SpringerLink, Taylor & Francis, and CABI, covering the period 2010–2025. The study followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to ensure methodological rigor and transparency. Automated procedures were employed, including an integrated R-based approach for bibliographic record merging and deduplication using an automated method, and an automated IF function-based screening process. The results reveal a growing trend in ecotourism-related research within geoparks. The most influential publications primarily focus on visitor motivations and preferences, ecotourism products and visitor experiences, and community-based ecotourism, as well as conservation, environmental education, and sustainable geopark management. While geotourism continues to occupy a central position in geopark development, the findings suggest that ecotourism can complement geotourism by promoting environmental responsibility, conservation awareness, community participation, and the broader sustainable development objectives of geopark territories.

Title: Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis: A Bibliometric Review using Bibliometrix to Map Research Trends and Algorithm Methods
Abstract: This study presents a bibliometric overview of research trends and algorithmic models in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA). Data were collected from the Scopus database, resulting in a dataset of 2,344 journal articles published between 2021 and early 2026. The analysis was conducted using the Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny packages in R to perform number of publications per year, source’s production over time, country production over time, keyword co-occurrence, thematic mapping and evolution of research themes. The results show that ABSA research has experienced rapid growth with an annual publication increase of more than 30%. This study identifies BERT algorithmic models and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) as the most dominant supporting tools in the research literature. Thematic maps show that transformer-based techniques and attention mechanisms have emerged as key driving themes in this field. Furthermore, thematic evolution maps reveal a shift in focus from technical aspect extraction to online public opinion analysis, reinforced by the sharp surge in the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in recent years. The findings provide a structured overview of the intellectual landscape of ABSA, clarifying dominant research clusters, methodological trajectories, and emerging themes. By highlighting the central role of transformer architectures, graph-based neural networks, and LLM integration, this study offers methodological guidance for future model development. Furthermore, the bibliometric insights reduce research fragmentation and identify underexplored directions, offering valuable insights for researchers to identify research gaps and develop more advanced ABSA models in future studies.

Title: Cartografía de la capacidad de innovación: Un estudio bibliométrico mediante Bibliometrix y visualización con VOSviewer
Abstract: Objetivo: El presente estudio busca analizar la estructura intelectual y la evolución temática en el campo de la capacidad de innovación en organizaciones, destacando su relevancia para el desempeño empresarial. Metodología: Se analizaron 614 artículos de la base de datos Scopus mediante herramientas bibliométricas como Bibliometrix y VOSviewer, lo que permitió visualizar las redes conceptuales y las tendencias en la producción científica. Resultados: Se muestra un notable crecimiento de la producción científica en los últimos años en el campo temático. Los países con mayor contribución son China, Indonesia y EE. UU., destacando la consolidación del continente asiático en la investigación sobre innovación. El análisis temático permitió identificar siete clústeres principales: innovación y desempeño, ventaja competitiva, capital y emprendimiento, absorción tecnológica, transformación digital, innovación en China y procesos y productos. Conclusión: Se concluye que la capacidad de innovación se vincula estrechamente con el liderazgo transformacional, las capacidades dinámicas y la gestión del conocimiento, siendo un factor clave para el rendimiento competitivo, especialmente en pymes. Se recomienda que futuras investigaciones analicen sectores económicos específicos y la bibliometría la complementen con revisiones sistemáticas y estudios empíricos.

Title: Virtual Tour Research Trends in Education: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis Using Bibliometrix R and Biblioshiny
Abstract: This study systematically examines the landscape of virtual tour research in education from 2020 to 2026 using a combined approach of systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix R and Biblioshiny. The research aims to identify publication trends, conceptual and thematic structures, intellectual patterns, and research gaps. Data were collected from Scopus-indexed journal articles, filtered using inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed through co-citation, co-occurrence, and thematic mapping. Results indicate rapid growth in publication volume, from 22 articles in 2020 to 135 in 2025, with interdisciplinary contributions spanning tourism, cultural heritage, urban studies, and educational technology. Intellectual and conceptual structures remain fragmented, with dominant themes on tourism, heritage, and facility-oriented training, whereas pedagogical strategies, assessment, and learning transfer are underexplored. Keyword co-occurrence reveals a reliance on virtual reality frameworks while emerging themes include responsible AI, digital twins, and ethics, suggesting a shift toward socially and ethically informed research directions. Findings highlight that virtual tours have transitioned from niche technological tools to integral pedagogical instruments, yet pedagogical applications require further consolidation. The study contributes to the field by mapping research evolution, identifying knowledge gaps, and guiding future research agendas toward systematic, pedagogically beneficial applications in education.

title: Virtual Tour Research Trends in Education: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis Using Bibliometrix R and Biblioshiny
abstract: This study systematically examines the landscape of virtual tour research in education from 2020 to 2026 using a combined approach of systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix R and Biblioshiny. The research aims to identify publication trends, conceptual and thematic structures, intellectual patterns, and research gaps. Data were collected from Scopus-indexed journal articles, filtered using inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed through co-citation, co-occurrence, and thematic mapping. Results indicate rapid growth in publication volume, from 22 articles in 2020 to 135 in 2025, with interdisciplinary contributions spanning tourism, cultural heritage, urban studies, and educational technology. Intellectual and conceptual structures remain fragmented, with dominant themes on tourism, heritage, and facility-oriented training, whereas pedagogical strategies, assessment, and learning transfer are underexplored. Keyword co-occurrence reveals a reliance on virtual reality frameworks while emerging themes include responsible AI, digital twins, and ethics, suggesting a shift toward socially and ethically informed research directions. Findings highlight that virtual tours have transitioned from niche technological tools to integral pedagogical instruments, yet pedagogical applications require further consolidation. The study contributes to the field by mapping research evolution, identifying knowledge gaps, and guiding future research agendas toward systematic, pedagogically beneficial applications in education.

Title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Entrepreneurial Intention: Insights from VOSViewer and RStudio Bibliometrix (2004-2024)
Abstract: The goal of this review is to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the study associated with entrepreneurial intention. The analysis includes a total numbers of 1,727 papers published between 2004 and 2024. The research aims to identify trends related to entrepreneurial purpose, the leading journals in this field, prolific authors, and the countries that are most frequently cited. The co-authorship network-map, intercountry co-authorship network map, and keyword co-occurrence maps are consequently provided. Scopus database was used to evaluate the substantial data regarding the numerous Publications incorporated into this investigation. A co-authorship map, an inter-country co-authorship network map, and a keyword co-occurrence network map were produced using the VOSviewer software. RStudio software was employed in this investigation to analyze the most prominent journals, prolific authors, countries' scientific production, and word maps of keywords and prevalent topics. The study's findings demonstrate that Education and Training is the most significant journal, with the highest no. of papers published in the Year 2024. Additionally, the most distinguished author is “Francisco Linan” with 21 papers, and the most cited country is Spain with 5134 citations. The word map of keywords shows the term "entrepreneur" occurs most frequently in the data set.The study enhances the existing body of literature regarding entrepreneurial intention. Bibliometric methodologies present a complete and reliable overview of this field. The findings may assist authors in seeking further research on this subject. The paper claims that it is the most valuable bibliometric study on entrepreneurial intention, offering current insights through the use of both Vosviewer and Rstudio software to facilitate a more comprehensive understanding.

Title: A Bibliometric Mapping of AI-Based Assistants in Software Engineering Using Bibliometrix and the Scopus Dataset (2014–2025)
Abstract: Artificial intelligence-based assistants have been developing at an incredible pace in recent years, facilitating fast information retrieval, automating repetitive tasks, and improving operational efficiency. In the field of software engineering, these tools now assist in activities such as testing, code generation, and documentation. Despite the increasing recognition of artificial intelligence (AI) as a valuable element of software development, its overall contributions remain insufficiently characterized. This research conducts a bibliometric analysis of AI-based assistants in the context of software development, identifying key publications, leading authors and organizations, and underexplored areas where these tools have a significant impact. As a result of a literature search conducted using the Scopus database, 83 papers (2014–2025) were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package for bibliometric evaluation. The collected documents revealed a sustained annual growth rate of 24.14%, with a peak in 2024 (31 papers), reflecting the surge in generative AI and LLM-based tools. The most cited article received 118 citations (39.33 citations per year), highlighting a strong impact in recent contributions. The United States led in publications with 26.1%, while Europe had the highest citation impact with 73 citations. Software design is the dominant theme with 41 papers and 19% of occurrences, while keyword trends focus on language models (LLM) with 19 papers, chatbots with 18 papers, and LLMs with 11 papers, confirming a clear shift toward LLM-centered research in software engineering. It provides insights into future research directions and opportunities for AI-driven innovation in software development .

Title: Who is Leading the Housing Satisfaction Study: A Bibliometric Analysis based on Bibliometrix Tools and CiteSpace
Abstract: Due to its significant implications for individual well-being, community cohesion, and socio-economic development, housing satisfaction has increasingly become a critical topic in urban studies, sociology, and public policy. In 2023 alone, 149 articles related to housing satisfaction were indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (with a cumulative total of 1,383 articles as of August 15, 2024). While these contributions enrich the research field, they also present challenges of information overload and difficulty in filtering relevant studies for application. Consequently, this study employs bibliometric methods to analyze the performance of existing research, focusing on key actors and influential works from five perspectives: country/region, institutions, authorship, publication sources, and citation metrics. Additionally, it categorizes the main branches of housing satisfaction research based on terminological standards to assist stakeholders in quickly identifying potential opportunities for support, collaboration, and citation. The results indicate that the United States and China dominate the field nationally, with institutions such as the Ohio University System and Hong Kong Baptist University forming the core research collaboration networks. At the author level, Hur Misun, Mouratidis Kostas, and Lu Max emerge as the most influential authors in terms of cumulative impact, short-term influence, and citation frequency, respectively. In terms of research branches, the most concentrated topics include residential satisfaction, housing satisfaction, and neighborhood satisfaction. The study also reveals that the research collaboration network in this field is relatively fragmented, with a reliance on traditional data sources and methods, and an overly concentrated distribution of research topics

Title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Industry 4.0 in Procurement Decision Making Using VOS Viewer and R Studio Bibliometrix
Abstract: Purpose: This study aims to map and evaluate the emerging body of research on Industry 4.0 in procurement to clarify its intellectual structure, dominant themes, and future research directions. Design/methodology/approach: 66 documents were selected using Elsevier Scopus. Analysis was conducted using bibliometric and science mapping techniques implemented in R (Biblioshiny). This analysis examined publication trends, collaboration patterns, influential authors, and thematic structures within the field. Findings: The results highlight the publication trend and reveal that this research domain is growing rapidly but is fragmented, with limited contributions from countries, journals, and authors. Thematic and network analysis reveal a strong emphasis on technology adoption and performance outcomes, whereas views on procurement strategy, organization, and sustainability have yet to be deeply explored. Originality: This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric overview of Industry 4.0 in procurement research, a field that remains underexplored within the broader digital supply chain literature. Implications: This study helps not only in the expansion of the knowledge base on the research topic but also in understanding the evolution of the industry 4.0 and procurement, providing research support further in this area.

Title: Systematic Literature Review: Ethnomathematics Research Trends Using Bibliometrix R Studio Biblioshiny (2005-2025)
Abstract: This study aims to analyze the trend of scientific publications on the theme of ethnomathematics indexed by Scopus during the period 2005-2025. The analysis is conducted as a basis for identifying future research directions and opportunities. The method used is Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the help of bibliometric analysis using R Studio through the biblioshiny interface. Data was collected automatically through the Scopus API with the keyword “ethnomathematics”, which resulted in 670 documents from journals, books, book chapters and others. Furthermore, publication patterns, author collaboration, journal distribution, and thematic trends were analyzed. Data visualization through biblioshiny provides a comprehensive picture of research dynamics, which can be used as a strategic reference for the development of further studies in this field. Trends in the topics of equations, ethnomathematics, mathematics education, and curricul from the derivatives of this theme are also still largely unexamined so it is important that there is novelty related to further research on the theme of ethnomathematics.

Title: Sustentabilidade Rural: Uma análise bibliométrica da produção científica a partir das metodologias de avaliação, utilizando a ferramenta bibliometrix R
Abstract: Rural sustainability is a topic of growing global importance,encompassing environmental, economic, and social aspects of agricultural development. This study aimed to analyze the development of global scientific production on sustainability assessment methodologies for the agricultural sector between 1991 and 2024. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using bibliometrix R based on the Web of Science database. A total of 725 documents on “Sustainable Rural Development” and 724 documents on sustainability assessment tools were identified. The main results revealed an average annual growth rate of 13.43% in scientific production, with emphasis on the journals Journal of Rural Studies and Journal of Cleaner Production. China, Spain, and Brazil lead in publications, while European institutions dominate tool development. The study’s contribution lies in the systematic mapping of the literature and the identification of gaps, such as the invisibility of the Global South in discussions on assessment methodologies.

Title: The Navigating the Data Labyrinth: A Bibliometrix of Data Governance Challenges in Implementing Digital Twins for Disaster Management in Developing Countries
Abstract: Indonesia faces significant disaster risks due to its location in the Ring of Fire, necessitating advanced mitigation technologies like Digital Twins (DT). However, the effectiveness of DT relies heavily on real-time data integration, which is often hindered by governance issues rather than technological capability. This study aims to identify specific data governance challenges in adopting DT for the public sector specifically in disaster management and proposes a conceptual framework suitable for developing countries, using Indonesia as the primary representative case. A Bibliometric analysis was conducted using the PRISMA protocol. Data was collected from Scopus (n=107) and Google Scholar/PoP, covering the period 2018–2026, focusing on the intersection of Digital Twin, Disaster Management, and Data Governance. Additionally, a qualitative case study approach was employed, utilizing Indonesia as the primary representation of developing countries to validate the proposed framework. The study identifies three key challenge dimensions: (1) Organizational (data silos and ownership ambiguity), (2) Technical (semantic interoperability and legacy systems), and (3) Legal-Ethical (data privacy and sovereignty). The paper proposes the "Integrated Disaster Data Governance for Digital Twin (IDDG-DT)" framework, which aligns with the Satu Data Indonesia policy, emphasizing that robust data governance is a prerequisite for successful Digital Twin implementation.

Title: A mixed methods analysis of artificial intelligence ethics discourse evolution in the generative era using bibliometrix and BERTopic
Abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced novel risks, including deepfakes and algorithmic hallucinations, urgently demanding a fundamental shift in global AI ethics from theoretical presuppositions toward actionable governance practices. By uncovering the developmental trajectory of ethical discourse in the era of generative AI, this study conducts a systematic analysis of the existing literature, aiming to generate actionable insights for future interdisciplinary research and contribute to the reconstruction of a renewed ethical order in this field. To this end, this study constructs a mixed-methods framework integrating macro-level bibliometrics with the micro-level BERTopic deep semantic mining approach. Following a structured multi-stage screening protocol, this paper performs a quantitative analysis of 1,190 core documents (2020–2025) retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases, identifying 10 core themes and examining their spatio-temporal evolution.The findings reveal that 2023 represents a pivotal turning point in generative AI ethics research ; by 2025, the human-centered theme of ‘education and cognitive literacy’ had surpassed the long-dominant topic of ‘law and governmental regulation’ in publication volume. This shift suggests a reorientation in global governance discourse from a defensive emphasis on ‘technical compliance’ toward an adaptive focus on ‘human-centered cognitive empowerment’. Furthermore, global knowledge production exhibits a pronounced “center-periphery” structure, where a small group of developed countries dominates agenda-setting, while the Global South remains in a marginal position ; meanwhile, the academic literature tends to cluster into two distinguishable discursive orientations: one centered on ‘technical governance’ and the other on ‘humanistic reflection’. This study calls for bridging the binary epistemological divide by integrating humanistic values into technological instrumental rationality, while broadening the current discourse framework and addressing structural imbalances through more inclusive North-South collaboration, with the ultimate goal of advancing global ‘epistemic justice’ in the era of generative AI.

Title: Mapping the Intellectual Structure of Climate Change Vulnerability and Resilience Research (2020–2026): A Bibliometric Analysis Using the Bibliometrix R Package
Abstract: Risk, vulnerability, and resilience have become central concepts across disaster studies, climate adaptation, development, public health, urban planning, and economic policy. This study maps the recent intellectual, conceptual, and social structure of research that connects these concepts with developing and emerging economies. A corpus of 560 English-language records published between 2020 and 2026 was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and analysed with the bibliometrix package in R. Performance analysis was combined with author, source, country, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, thematic, and reference co-citation analyses. The corpus comprised 312 sources and displayed an annual growth rate of 16.02%, an average of 14.99 citations per document, 3.94 co-authors per document, and 38.21% international co-authorship. China and India contributed the largest numbers of corresponding-author publications, while Sustainability and the International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction were the most productive sources. Climate change, adaptation, disaster management, and sustainability formed the dominant conceptual core, whereas agriculture, food security, poverty, adaptive capacity, and governance constituted a more applied livelihood-oriented strand. The keyword communities were only weakly separated, indicating overlap rather than discrete subfields. The country network also showed multiple collaboration groupings, but these patterns should not be treated as direct evidence of research leadership or funding dependence. Co-citation results indicated a substantially shared intellectual foundation rooted in vulnerability assessment, social–ecological resilience, community resilience, and disaster-risk scholarship. The study shows a rapidly expanding and interdisciplinary literature in which climate-related concerns are prominent, while also identifying opportunities for stronger integration across policy, institutional, household, and livelihood scales.

Title: Research Trends in Non-Pharmacological Interventions and Traditional Medicine Body Constitution: A Preregistered Two-Branch Bibliometric Analysis of Web of Science and CNKI Literature Using bibliometrix, 2000–2025
Abstract: This preregistered bibliometric study maps research on non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) in which Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) body constitution (中医体质), typically assessed with the Constitution in Chinese Medicine Questionnaire (CCMQ), is substantively involved. NPIs include acupuncture-moxibustion and acupoint stimulation, tuina and other manual therapies, traditional mind-body exercise (e.g., Tai Chi, Baduanjin, Qigong), general exercise, psychological and emotional interventions, dietary interventions, and lifestyle, health-education and constitution-based nursing programs. Because Chinese- and English-language bibliographic databases differ in metadata structure, the study runs two parallel, non-merged branches with the same analytical settings: Branch A (international literature, Web of Science Core Collection) and Branch B (Chinese literature, CNKI academic journals). bibliometrix (R) is the core analytical engine in both branches, VOSviewer produces all network maps with identical parameters, and CiteSpace is used for burst detection. PubMed is used only to audit search coverage. The study describes publication growth, contributors and collaboration, the intervention landscape (which NPIs are studied for which constitution types), thematic evolution across three policy-anchored periods, the evidence profile and the use of CCMQ, and the intellectual base of the international literature, and it compares the two branches. It is descriptive: it makes no causal claims and does not assess efficacy or quality of evidence.

Title: Bibliometrix analysis using biblioShiny in R package of "digital transformation and organizational change" extracted from both web of science and Scopus
Abstract: The abundant literature on the subject of organizational change clearly demonstrates the great interest that practitioners and researchers have in the subject. In a context of perpetual change, organizations find themselves obliged to study and develop their ability to adapt to change in order to ensure their survival. It is for this reason that a great deal of research is being carried out in this area, attempting to provide managers and leaders with models of change adapted to the context of digital innovation and digital transformation. In this article, we have attempted to present the state of the art of research through a bibliometric analysis using the R tool Biblioshiny of the corpus consisting of 85 articles combined from the renowned databases SCOPUS and WEB OF SCIENCE. The highlight we conclude from this combined analysis is: that developed countries continue to invest in digital technologies and therefore by default in the issues to be mobilized to develop the capacity to change. The construct linking digital transformation, organisational change and innovation implies that digital transformation is the result of a technological innovation that requires managerial innovation to succeed, just as it can just as easily be the result of an organizational innovation following organizational and leadership change, so the dynamics of change are transversal. The phenomenon of digital transformation has more of a managerial and organizational framework than a technical one, since it is people who are the final receivers and the main players, hence the interest in managerial and social journals. The findings of this study will be of interest for both researchers and managers who work on the phenomenon of digital transformation and organizational change
